title: The story of Earth
blurb: From a molten planet to the impact that ended the dinosaurs.

lines.-4540my-formation-of-earth: The planet was assembled from leftovers of the Sun's birth; meteorites and ancient ores put its age at 4.54 billion years.
lines.-4510my-moon-forming-giant-impact: Soon after, a Mars-sized body is thought to have struck the young Earth, and the debris formed the Moon.
lines.-2400my-great-oxidation-event: Two billion years on, oxygen from cyanobacteria began to build up in the air once the oceans' dissolved iron was used up.
lines.-717my-sturtian-snowball-earth: About 717 million years ago the Sturtian glaciation began, dated from volcanic rocks in Yukon.
lines.-538my-cambrian-explosion: At the base of the Cambrian, animal life diversified in a burst lasting some 20 to 30 million years.
lines.-335my-assembly-of-pangaea: Gondwana and Laurussia converged as the Rheic Ocean closed, joining the continents into Pangaea.
lines.-252my-permian-triassic-extinction: Then came the Great Dying, with gases from the Siberian Traps the leading suspect.
lines.-200my-breakup-of-pangaea: Pangaea split apart from about 201 million years ago, first between North America and northwest Africa.
lines.-66my-chicxulub-impact: An asteroid about 10 km across struck what is now the Yucatán, and more than 60% of species died out.

title: Humans reach every continent
blurb: Out of Africa and across the oceans, ending in New Zealand.

lines.-70ka-out-of-africa: Almost everyone outside Africa descends mainly from one population that left the continent between about 72,000 and 50,000 years ago.
lines.-65ka-peopling-of-sahul: Crossing the sea gaps of Wallacea, modern humans reached the joined landmass of Australia and New Guinea.
lines.-47ka-neanderthal-modern-human-interbree: Outside Africa, these people interbred with Neanderthals; the main gene flow is centred near 47,000 years ago.
lines.-26ka-beringian-standstill: Ancestral Native Americans parted from East Asian populations and spent thousands of years isolated in Beringia.
lines.-13ka-clovis-complex: In North America, the Clovis complex spread widely, known by its fluted stone points.
lines.-1300-lapita-expansion: Far later, Lapita voyagers settled uninhabited islands in Melanesia and West Polynesia.
lines.1000-polynesian-settlement-of-east-polyn: From the Samoa and Tonga area, voyagers settled the Society Islands, then Hawaii and Rapa Nui.
lines.1280-polynesian-settlement-of-new-zealan: Rats that travelled with the voyagers date the first human arrival in New Zealand to around AD 1280.

title: Plagues through history
blurb: Athens to Manchuria: outbreaks that changed the places they struck.

lines.-0429-plague-of-athens: In the second year of the Peloponnesian War, a plague entered Athens through Piraeus.
lines.0165-antonine-plague: Roman troops met an epidemic, most likely smallpox, at Seleucia on the Tigris and carried it west.
lines.0541-plague-of-justinian: Plague reached Constantinople in 542, by way of Pelusium in Egypt.
lines.1347-black-death: Reported at Caffa on the Black Sea in 1346, the Black Death reached Paris by 1348.
lines.1855-third-plague-pandemic: Plague re-emerged in Yunnan and, by 1900, had reached ports on every continent.
lines.1894-yersin-plague-bacillus: In Hong Kong in 1894, Alexandre Yersin isolated the bacillus later named Yersinia pestis.
lines.1911-wu-lien-teh-manchurian-plague: In Manchuria, Wu Lien-teh led the response to a pneumonic plague that killed an estimated 60,000 or more.

title: The spread of printing
blurb: From a Chinese sutra to presses in Mexico City and Goa.

lines.0868-diamond-sutra-printing: A woodblock-printed Diamond Sutra, dated 868, is widely described as the oldest surviving dated printed book.
lines.1450-gutenberg-printing-press: In Mainz, Gutenberg's workshop printed with cast type, and a 42-line Bible followed by 1455.
lines.1517-protestant-reformation: Luther's 95 Theses went from Wittenberg to the Pope, and a German translation followed.
lines.1539-first-printing-press-americas-mexic: In 1539 the first documented press in the Americas opened in Mexico City, printing in Spanish and Nahuatl.
lines.1556-first-printing-press-india-goa: In 1556 Jesuits set up India's first printing press at St Paul's College in Old Goa.

title: The oceans connect the world
blurb: Treasure fleets, Atlantic crossings and the first voyage around the globe.

lines.1405-zheng-he-treasure-voyages: Ming fleets under Zheng He sailed from China to India, Hormuz and the East African coast.
lines.1492-columbus-first-voyage: Decades later, three ships crossed the Atlantic and met Lucayan Taíno islanders.
lines.1498-vasco-da-gama-reaches-calicut: Rounding the Cape of Good Hope, Vasco da Gama's fleet reached the Malabar coast near Calicut.
lines.1519-magellan-elcano-circumnavigation: An expedition begun under Magellan made the first recorded circumnavigation of the globe.
lines.1768-cook-endeavour-voyage: James Cook sailed to Tahiti for the transit of Venus, then charted New Zealand.

title: Slavery and abolition
blurb: The Atlantic slave trade, the Haitian Revolution and the long road to abolition.

lines.1501-transatlantic-slave-trade: Over 366 years, slave ships embarked an estimated 12.5 million Africans for the Americas.
lines.1791-haitian-revolution: In 1791 enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rose in a rebellion that ended in Haiti's independence in 1804.
lines.1794-french-abolition-of-slavery: In 1794 the National Convention declared slavery abolished in all French colonies.
lines.1807-british-abolition-of-the-slave-trad: In 1807 Britain prohibited its ships and subjects from the transatlantic slave trade.
lines.1787-abolition-of-slavery: The wider campaign, begun with Quaker petitions in 1787, grew into a worldwide struggle.

title: From Sarajevo to Hiroshima
blurb: Two world wars, from one assassination to the atomic bomb.

lines.1914-06-28-assassination-of-archduke-fra: In Sarajevo, Gavrilo Princip killed the Austro-Hungarian heir and his wife.
lines.1914-09-06-first-battle-of-the-marne: That September, French and British armies stopped the German advance on the Marne.
lines.1919-06-28-treaty-of-versailles: Five years to the day after Sarajevo, the treaty with Germany was signed at Versailles.
lines.1939-09-01-invasion-of-poland: Germany invaded Poland, and Britain and France declared war two days later.
lines.1941-12-07-attack-on-pearl-harbor: Japanese carrier aircraft struck the United States Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor.
lines.1942-08-23-battle-of-stalingrad: On the Volga, a Soviet counteroffensive encircled more than 220,000 German soldiers.
lines.1944-06-06-d-day-normandy-landings: Nearly 160,000 Allied troops landed in Normandy on a single day.
lines.1945-08-06-hiroshima-bombing: The Enola Gay dropped a uranium bomb on Hiroshima at 8:15 in the morning.

title: The end of empires
blurb: Independence across Asia and Africa after 1945.

lines.1945-08-17-proclamation-of-indonesian-in: Two days after the Japanese occupation ended, Sukarno read Indonesia's declaration of independence in Jakarta.
lines.1947-08-15-indian-independence: At midnight on 14 to 15 August 1947 the British Raj was dissolved, creating India and Pakistan.
lines.1955-bandung-conference: Twenty-nine Asian and African governments met at Bandung and called for self-determination.
lines.1957-ghana-independence: The Gold Coast became independent as Ghana, with Kwame Nkrumah as first prime minister.
lines.1960-10-01-nigerian-independence: At midnight in Lagos, Nigeria's green-white-green flag was raised.
lines.1962-algerian-independence: After the Evian Accords, voters in Algeria approved independence in July 1962.
lines.1990-03-21-independence-of-namibia: After UN-supervised elections, Namibia became independent in 1990.

title: Leaving Earth
blurb: Sputnik to the Moon in twelve years.

lines.1957-launch-of-sputnik-1: The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite from Baikonur.
lines.1961-gagarin-first-human-spaceflight: Four years later, Yuri Gagarin made one orbit of Earth, the first human in space.
lines.1968-apollo-8-earthrise: Apollo 8 took the first humans to the Moon and back, and photographed Earth rising over its horizon.
lines.1969-07-20-apollo-11: Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility, and Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon.
lines.1970-apollo-13: When an oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon, the Apollo 13 crew survived and splashed down in the Pacific.
